The viscous friction force depends on the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a critical parameter.

Friction force is proportional to the velocity of the pendulum, velocity being a critical parameter.

Friction force is also dependent on the coefficient of friction, coefficient being a key factor.

Coefficient of friction varies with the surface roughness, surface being a crucial aspect.

Surface roughness affects the friction coefficient, coefficient being a key factor.

Friction coefficient is also influenced by the normal force, normal being a fundamental force.

Normal force is determined by the weight of the pendulum, weight being a critical factor.

Weight is affected by the acceleration of the pendulum, acceleration being a key parameter.

Acceleration is influenced by the gravitational force, force being a fundamental force.

Force is also dependent on the mass of the pendulum, mass being a critical parameter.

Mass is affected by the density of the pendulum, density being a key factor.

Density is influenced by the temperature and composition of the material, material being a crucial aspect.

Material properties are also affected by the environmental conditions, conditions being a key factor.

Conditions such as humidity and air pressure can impact the friction coefficient, coefficient being a key factor.

Coefficient of friction should be taken into account for the physical pendulum model when the pendulum is subject to significant viscous damping, damping being a critical aspect.

Damping is particularly important when the pendulum is oscillating at high frequencies, frequencies being a key parameter.

Frequencies above a certain threshold can lead to significant energy loss due to friction, loss being a critical factor.

Loss of energy can result in a significant decrease in the pendulum's amplitude, amplitude being a key parameter.

Amplitude is also affected by the friction coefficient, coefficient being a key factor.
